limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The result answers the arbitrary-vector question in arXiv:2609.20346v1 by combining a known polynomial defect identity with the zero-defect Lévy face decomposition, then derives a countable tomography theorem. It does not claim those prior ingredients, Hausdorff moment uniqueness, disintegration, or Fourier uniqueness as new. The trace maps are L2 extensions rather than pointwise boundary traces; Lévy measures alone do not recover boundary-supported defining mass, for which the drift is essential. Older completely-hyperexpansive model literature may contain equivalent one-variable trace formulations.
record_title: All-vector Lévy measures and measure tomography in bidisc Dirichlet spaces
